recentItems.title: Orange Order parade row distracts from Northern Ireland’s everyday concerns
recentItems.description:
A dispute over a Protestant parade through a mainly Catholic neighbourhood in Northern Ireland has reignited old divisions. 
But some say the dispute is taking attention away from more pressing issues - including long hospital waiting lists, pressure on public services and a shortage of affordable homes. 

Al Jazeera’s Milena Veselinovic reports from Belfast, Northern Ireland.

recentItems.title: Lebanon’s Kfar Shouba lives under Israeli military orders
recentItems.description:
Residents of Kfar Shouba in southern Lebanon say they are living under direct Israeli military orders. 
The town sits along the border with Israel. 
While it is not among the dozens of villages occupied by Israeli forces, locals say troops regularly carry out cross-border incursions and, at times, detain people.

Al Jazeera’s Zeina Khodr reports from Kfar Shouba, southern Lebanon.

recentItems.title: Freed Syrians allege torture in Israeli detention as families await answers
recentItems.description:

While some detainees are released within hours, 51 Syrians are currently held in Israel.
There's no information on their whereabouts, charges, or health.

Al Jazeera’s Heidi Pett has been speaking to those who have been released.

recentItems.title: Israeli settlers shoot three Palestinian farmers in West Bank pogrom
recentItems.description:
There have been attacks by Israeli settlers and raids by Israel's military across the occupied West Bank on Wednesday morning.
A Palestinian was killed in an attack by Israeli settlers accompanied by soldiers in the town of Burqa, north of Nablus.
Settlers also shot and injured three Palestinian farmers in the village of Ramin.
And in nearby Tulkarem, Israeli forces raided the city and arrested two Palestinians. 

Al Jazeera’s Nida Ibrahim reports from Ramallah, occupied West Bank.

recentItems.title: Saudi Arabia wary of testing Mecca pact as Yemen war returns, analyst says
recentItems.description:
Sultan Barakat, a senior professor in public policy at Qatar Foundation’s Hamad Bin Khalifa University, told Al Jazeera that Yemen has pretty much returned to civil war as fighting has intensified in the past week, following years of a stalemate.

With the Saudi-backed internationally-recognised Yemeni government now recording some gains against the Houthis, Barakat said it would be hard to envision a break in the fighting.

But while Saudi Arabia has taken a “more aggressive posture” against the Houthis, Barakat said the kingdom is still wary of being too deeply involved.

“It’s not in their interest to get involved in a prolonged conflict in Yemen,” he said. “They have other priorities economically, regionally, in terms of security alliances, etc. So they don’t want to waste their assets in this particular moment.”

Saudi Arabia might also be reluctant to test its new security pact with Pakistan and Turkiye, Barakat added, so as not to expose its limitations.

Riyadh also has other defence priorities as regards Iran and Israel, he noted.

However, if the Houthis were to take the strategic city of Taiz, a gateway to the Aden base of the Saudi-backed coalition forces, then Riyadh might react more forcefully, Barakat concluded.

recentItems.title: Israel marks three years since October 7 as Gaza attacks continue despite ceasefire
recentItems.description:
Israelis are gathering across the country to mark three years since the October the 7th attacks.
At least 1,195 people were killed when Hamas and other Palestinian groups stormed the border.
One of the sites attacked was a music festival in Kfar Azza in southern Israel.
On Wednesday, friends and relatives of the victims gathered to pay their respects.
During the event, loud bangs could be heard from Gaza where the Israeli military is carrying out attacks despite a ceasefire. 

Overnight in Gaza, at least one person was killed in Israeli attacks. 
He was a member of the civil defence agency and was trying to rescue injured people near a hospital when Israeli aircraft bombed the area again.
After three years of genocide, Israeli attacks have killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, roughly 1,500 of them during the ceasefire.
Most of Gaza's population is still displaced and living in tents or destroyed buildings across the strip.

Al Jazeera’s Hani Mahmoud reports from Gaza City.

recentItems.title: The story of the “Palestine” football team without Palestinian players | Al Jazeera World
recentItems.description:
In 1934, a team called Palestine entered the qualifying rounds of the football World Cup in Mussolini’s fascist Italy. But it did not include any Palestinian players. It was drawn largely from the Jewish sporting movement under the British Mandate, at a time when football reflected the changing face of Palestine.

This documentary uncovers the forgotten history of Mandate-era football - how British rule, Zionist organisation and Palestinian exclusion shaped the makeup of the first team to compete internationally as Palestine. Through archives, interviews with specialist historians and the story of the 1934 qualifiers against Egypt, the film traces how the established football association became Israel’s, while Palestinian football was plagued by revolt, war and the 1948 Nakba. Decades later, Palestinians fought to reclaim their place in world football, finally securing FIFA recognition in 1998.

Original film title: Palestine: The Lost Team
